name: Dream11
summary: Dream11 is the best-known product of Dream Sports, a sports technology company whose platforms see sharp traffic peaks around live matches. Candidates commonly report coding, problem-solving and system design rounds for engineers, and conversations around the group's published DOPUT values: Data Driven, Ownership, Perseverance, User First and Transparency.
rounds: Online or live coding round for engineering roles (often)
System design for experienced engineers, often around scale and traffic spikes
Hiring manager round on past work and ownership
Culture or HR conversation, often around the DOPUT values
looks_for: Designing for sudden traffic peaks around match start times
Understanding sports fans and how they use the product

questions.text: Tell me about a decision you made based on data that went against your first instinct.
covers: What you first believed and why
The data you looked at and how you checked it was sound
The decision you made and how it turned out

questions.text: Tell me about a problem you owned end to end, from spotting it to fixing it for good.
covers: How you noticed it and why you took it on
The steps you drove yourself, and who you pulled in
The lasting fix and how you checked it held

questions.text: Describe a time you kept going on something hard after your first attempts failed.
covers: Why the problem was hard and what you tried first
What you changed after each failure, not just trying harder
Where it ended up, including if it was only partly solved

questions.text: Tell me about a time you shared bad news early with your team or manager.
covers: What the news was and why it would have been easy to wait
How and when you raised it, with the facts and options
What raising it early made possible

questions.text: Describe a time you changed what you were building after seeing how users actually used it.
covers: What you planned and what users really did
How you learned it: data, feedback, watching sessions
What you changed and the effect on users

questions.text: Lineups are announced shortly before a match, and many users edit their teams in the last minutes. How would you design for that rush?
covers: Estimating the peak and separating reads (player data) from writes (team saves)
Caching, queues and autoscaling ahead of known match times
Locking teams cleanly at the deadline, and what degrades first under strain

questions.text: How would you design a live leaderboard that updates points for a very large contest as the match happens?
covers: Turning match events into player points, then into team scores
Ranking at scale: sharding, sorted structures, updating in batches
Being honest in the UI about delay, and how the final result is confirmed

questions.text: A big match is a week away. How would you prepare the platform and the team for the expected peak?
covers: Capacity planning from past peaks, plus load tests at a higher level
A change freeze, runbooks and clear on-call roles for match day
What you'd switch off first if load exceeded the plan

questions.text: Explain how you'd use caching for match and player data, and what can go wrong when the cache is stale.
covers: What to cache and for how long, based on how often it changes
Invalidation when a lineup or score changes
Problems such as users seeing old data, and a thundering herd when a cache expires

questions.text: Many users drop off on the team-creation screen. How would you find out why and test a fix?
covers: Finding exactly where in the flow they leave, by device and type of user
Watching sessions or asking users, not only reading dashboards
One fix to test with a clear success metric and a guardrail

questions.text: How would you show that a new feature increased engagement, rather than just moving it from another part of the app?
covers: An A/B test or holdout group instead of a before-and-after view
Measuring total engagement per user, not just use of the new feature
Allowing for match schedules, since big games change behaviour on their own

questions.text: Why Dream Sports? Which of the DOPUT values describes how you like to work?
covers: A reason tied to sport, scale or the product, not only the brand
One value with a short, real example
What you want to learn or build here

questions.text: Which sport do you follow most closely, and what would you build for its fans?
covers: Genuine knowledge of how fans of that sport follow it
An idea framed around a fan's problem, not a feature list
How you'd know fans valued it

tips: Use the product as a fan would before the interview: build a team, follow it through a match and notice where the experience could improve.
In design rounds, start with the traffic shape: quiet most of the time, then a sharp peak near match start.
Prepare one story for each DOPUT value; Ownership and User First are easy to show with real examples.
Bring numbers to data-driven stories: what you measured, the baseline and the change.
Show you care about sport, but keep answers about users and outcomes, not just your favourite team.
